Demand for a ReactJS Redux Developer in the Market

The React JavaScript framework was open-sourced in May 2013 and quickly rose to popularity, surpassing JQuery, Angular, Backbone. Benefits of React include virtual DOM usage for better performance, improved JSX syntax, and a modular, component-based approach. React takes advantage of tools like Flux, Redux, and MobX to build richer client-side applications. Redux is an instrument for controlling data-state and UI-state in ReactJS Redux apps. Flux/React+Redux present ViewModel layer in MVVM pattern. Still, there are a lot of other technologies/stacks which are combined during web or mobile app development:

React JS Redux vs Flux

Redux React JS is suitable for Single Page Applications (SPAs) development, but its functionality allows to develop different websites and apps. Before you hire React Redux developer, check examples of projects created with this technology:

  • SoundCloud App
  • Pabla
  • Panther
  • Flickr & Yandex Feed
  • JSON Viewer, etc.

Many of the apps, viewers, and frames were also created with the help of a combination of React Flux Redux. Flux is a pattern used for coordination of an application state and it allows us to have separate stores for different types of data. Many experts state that Redux was inspired by this very pattern and is also called “Flux-like”, still, Redux doesn’t have stores, and all the changes and actions are done on a state tree.

The Popularity of Flux vs Redux

Results of comparison of Flux Redux in Google Trends

According to Google Trends for the last three years Flux was much more searched for and, thus, is more popular than Redux. Flux is widespread in Canada, North America, some countries of Europe, and India. Redux, in its turn, is also popular in North America.

Creating ReactJS App as an Experienced ReactJS Redux Developer

First, a junior React Redux developer may configure Babel, Webpack, NPM by yourself but React developers from Facebook created a cool command-line tool — create-react-app — that provides a development skeleton for a smoother, faster development. Once you create the base for your future app, pay attention to your file and folder structure. For small and middle-sized applications, combine files by structure; when the app is growing, store them by the entity.

For better project scaling, impose strict rules for building different structures and naming conventions. Take a look at an example of an action:

const SOME_ACTION_NAME = “entityName/SOME_ACTION_NAME”;

Below is the corresponding action creator:

const someActionName = actionData => ({ type: SOME_ACTION_NAME, actionData });

You could notice a correlation between action name and action creator naming: it saves you time when debugging and allows you to maintain a solid code standard. For actions that make HTTP requests, a junior React Redux developer could implement:

const SOME_ACTION_REQUEST = “entityName/SOME_ACTION_REQUEST”;

const SOME_ACTION_SUCCESS = … const SOME_ACTION_ERROR = …

The same scheme works for reducers. Apply some general rule that should be used by a junior React Redux developer and everybody else working on the project:

export const initialState = { // some initial state data }

Another thing – the usage of containers. This is the point where the React app connects to the Redux store: a junior React Redux developer uses selectors in the mapStateToProps function. Selectors get the state as an input parameter and return the required key from the state:

mapStateToProps = state => ({ firstItem: firstItemSelector(state), secondItem: secondItemSelector(state) });

Below are the selectors:

firstItemSelector = state => state.reducerOne.firstItem;

And from another selector file:

secondItem = state => state.reducerTwo.secondItem;

Tips from a ReactJS Redux Developer on How to Ease ReactJS Work Process

You could use a React Router library function like reselect to improve your selectors and not ask them to recompute the same data when you need them repeatedly. For performance improvements use methods from your library, such as recompose, which calls onlyUpdateForKeys. Try to use class-based components just for containers and components that could handle any kind of additional logic before being rendered. For type checking, a junior React Redux developer uses prop-type Facebook packages. To protect your component renders, try to describe in detail all possible prop types and their variations. Some optional tools that you may also explore include Facebook Flow or TypeScript. Also, pay attention to testing React Redux apps using Jest that will save you time while debugging apps or fixing issues.

React Redux Developer Responsibilities and Functions

A React Redux developer on your team develops new apps and features, as well as enhances existing ones, using React.js, Redux, Enzyme Webpack, and other related development tools. Working knowledge and skills in ReactJS and Redux tools is a must to accomplish the functions of this role.

The main responsibilities of a React Redux developer are:

  1. Develop and maintain front-end components and features using ReactJS, Redux, and other related tools
  2. Develop user-centric and responsive user-interfaces for various web applications and mobile platforms.
  3. Streamline and optimize the performance of front-end tools and components.
  4. Develop, assess, and improve unit testing processes.
  5. Incorporate and improve codebase documentation
  6. Contribute to the development community
  7. Develop and grow organizational knowledge about building tools and components using ReactJS, Redux, and similar tools.
